node.title: Re^3: How do I use 'which' in the hash-bang line? (updated x2)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Sorry, I got so caught up in the point I was trying to make - that Perl scans the shebang line even when running the script as perl test.pl - that I missed the limitation that the AM pointed out below, that you are right that #!/usr/bin/env perl -w does in fact not work when invoking the script via ./test.pl.

so that #!/usr/bin/env perl -w does not work

It does for me:

$ cat test.pl #!/usr/bin/env perl -wls print $x+undef; $ perl test.pl -x=5 Use of uninitialized value in addition (+) at test.pl line 2. 5

From [doc://perlrun]: 'The #! line is always examined for switches as the line is being parsed. ... Parsing of the #! switches starts wherever "perl" is mentioned in the line.'

(I'm not sure about the history of this feature at the moment.) Update: The description of this feature was in [https://perl5.git.perl.org/perl.git/blob/a0d0e21ea6ea90a22318550944fe6cb09ae10cda:/pod/perlrun.pod#l39|perl-5.000], although apparently the support for which options are supported there has changed, for example [doc://perl58delta#Miscellaneous-Changes|perl58delta] says "The command-line options -s and -F are now recognized on the shebang (#!) line." or [doc://perl5100delta#Miscellaneous|perl5100delta] says "The -C option can no longer be used on the #! line." (Although as [choroba] pointed out and as the docs say: "It wasn't working there anyway, since the standard streams are already set up at this point in the execution of the perl interpreter.")
